definition: Dragon NaturallySpeaking (also known as Dragon for PC, or DNS) is a speech recognition software package developed by Dragon Systems of Newton, Massachusetts, which was acquired in turn by Lernout & Hauspie Speech Products, Nuance Communications, and Microsoft.
details: It runs on Windows personal computers. Version 15 (Professional Individual and Legal Individual), which supports 32-bit and 64-bit editions of Windows 7, 8 and 10, was released in August 2016.

explainer.lead: Dragon NaturallySpeaking is a speech-recognition package for Windows PCs, letting spoken input be handled by software rather than typed. It is relevant to the history of consumer speech recognition and to people who want a speech-based way to use a computer.

tiers.eli5: Dragon NaturallySpeaking is like a computer helper that listens when you talk and works out what you said. You speak to a Windows PC, and the software recognizes your speech. Its full name is often shortened to DNS.
tiers.practitioner: DNS is applied as a speech-recognition package on Windows personal computers. Version 15 Professional Individual and Legal Individual supports 32-bit and 64-bit Windows 7, 8, and 10; check the operating system and architecture before choosing that release. It was released in August 2016, so those specifications should not be treated as support for every later Windows version.
tiers.paperLevel: Dragon NaturallySpeaking can be described as a Windows-hosted speech-recognition system: spoken input -> recognized output. It was developed by Dragon Systems, whose ownership later passed through Lernout & Hauspie Speech Products, Nuance Communications, and Microsoft. The supplied technical details identify supported Windows editions for version 15 but do not specify its recognition algorithm or accuracy.

explainer.example: A user running 64-bit Windows 10 opens Dragon Professional Individual 15 and speaks to the PC. DNS recognizes the spoken input, providing an alternative to entering everything through the keyboard.

usedIn.name: Dragon Professional Individual 15
usedIn.detail: A version 15 edition supporting 32-bit and 64-bit Windows 7, 8, and 10.

usedIn.name: Dragon Legal Individual 15
usedIn.detail: The Legal Individual edition released alongside Professional Individual in August 2016, with the same stated Windows support.

explainer.intuition: The basic idea is to make speech an input to a personal computer: instead of expressing everything through a keyboard, a user can speak and have DNS recognize the input.
howItWorks: Install a compatible DNS edition on a Windows personal computer.
For version 15, use a supported 32-bit or 64-bit edition of Windows 7, 8, or 10.
Provide spoken input while running the software.
DNS performs speech recognition on that input.
explainer.whyItMatters: It packages speech recognition for ordinary Windows personal computers, making speech a practical computer-input option. Its succession of owners also connects it to a longer commercial history of speech-recognition products.
misconceptions: It was not originally developed by Microsoft; Dragon Systems developed it before the later acquisitions.
Version 15's stated support covers Windows 7, 8, and 10, not every operating system.
DNS, Dragon for PC, and Dragon NaturallySpeaking refer to the same package rather than three separate products.
